sections.label: What makes a usable eval case
items: An input AND an explicit, checkable criterion: not an implicit "judge if it's good."
Deterministic checks (exact match, schema validation) wherever a fixed correct answer/shape exists.
LLM-as-judge reserved for genuinely subjective criteria with no deterministic check available.

sections.label: Regression definition
sections.formula: regression = (baseline is a real number) AND (new_score < baseline)

sections.label: Isolating variables
items: Change ONE thing (one prompt, one retrieval parameter), then re-run the full eval suite.
Changing several things and evaluating once tells you SOMETHING changed, not WHICH part.

sections.label: Deterministic vs. LLM-as-judge
items: Deterministic: consistent, cheap, exactly reproducible: always prefer when it applies.
LLM-as-judge: inherits the exact unreliability it's measuring, the judge's own grading is an unverified model output.

sections.label: Common mistakes
items: Spot-checking a handful of outputs instead of running a systematic, repeatable eval.
Not wrapping each check() call in its own try/except: one bad checker can crash the whole evaluation.
Changing multiple variables in one deploy, then evaluating once.

sections.label: Implementation checklist
checklist: Every eval case has an explicit pass/fail criterion, not an implicit judgment call.
model_fn and check() failures are each caught independently, never crashing the whole run.
A baseline score is recorded and compared before every ship.
